mission_06: Constraint-based learning incorporates domain knowledge as hard or soft constraints during model training. Monotonicity constraints ensure certain parameters stay non-negative (e.g., more experience should never decrease salary predictions). Ordering constraints enforce relationships between parameters (e.g., feature A should be more important than feature B). Sum constraints fix the total weight budget. The approach combines data-driven gradients with constraint satisfaction: soft constraints add penalty terms to the loss, while hard constraints project parameters onto feasible regions after each update. In this mission, you implement multiple constraint types (monotonic, sum_equals, ordering, sparsity), evaluate constraint satisfaction as continuous scores, compute numerical gradients for constraint penalties, and project parameters onto constraint-satisfying regions.
